title: What the Private Access, Internet Security, Digital Experience and Data Protection windows of the app show

prose.label: Endpoint DLP requirements.

prose.label: Endpoint DLP notifications.

prose.label: Exemption.
prose.text: {{dlp-exemption}} The length of an exemption is given two ways {{divergence:exemption-duration}}; the console setting is [[zia.dlp.endpoint-settings:exemption-duration]]. How a user enters exemption mode is partly answered here; whether it relates to the `zdpmode` log field and to the password that disables Endpoint DLP is still open [[zia.dlp.endpoint-settings:exemption-mode]].

private-access-classic.statement: The Classic Private Access window on Windows shows Username; Service Status, where Turn Off turns off the Zscaler Tunnel and disables the Private Access service while the user stays logged in, until Turn On; Authenticate Early, to reauthenticate Private Access before authentication expires; Time Connected; Network Type (Trusted Network, VPN-Trusted Network, Split VPN-Trusted Network or Off-Trusted Network); Authentication Status; Broker, the IP address of the server traffic is forwarded to; Client, the device's local IP address; Protocol (TLS or DTLS); and Total Bytes Sent and Total Bytes Received through the Z-Tunnel in real time.

evidence.after: This window includes the following features on Windows devices.
quotes: Username: Displays the username with which you are logged into the app.

Service Status: Displays the app connection status. Click Turn Off if you want to turn off the Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel) and disable the Private Access service while remaining logged in to the app. The Private Access service is disabled until you click Turn On.
Authenticate Early: Click Authenticate Early to reauthenticate Private Access before your authentication expires.
Time Connected: Displays your initial connection time for the present session.
Total Bytes Received: Displays, in real time, bytes of traffic received by your computer through the Z-Tunnel.
Network Type: Displays the type of network you are connected to (Trusted Network, VPN-Trusted Network, Split VPN-Trusted Network, or Off-Trusted Network).
Authentication Status: Displays the current authentication state (i.e., whether you are currently authenticated or not).
Broker: Displays the IP address of the server to which your traffic is being forwarded.
Client: Displays the local IP address of your device.
Protocol: Displays the protocol used for the tunnel (TLS or DTLS).
Total Bytes Sent: Displays, in real time, bytes of traffic sent from your computer through the Z-Tunnel.

vpn-tunnel-section.statement: The Classic Private Access window on macOS has a VPN Tunnel section that displays only when the device is connected to the Zscaler cloud using a VPN connection. On Windows the section is likewise displayed only then, and has these fields: VPN Service Edge, the IP address of the VPN Service Edge traffic is forwarded to (shown as Network Service Edge in previous versions); Client IP, the address the VPN Service Edge assigned for the session; and the bytes sent and received through the VPN Tunnel.

evidence.after: This window includes the following features on Windows devices.
quotes: This section displays only if you are connected to the Zscaler cloud using a VPN connection.
VPN Service Edge: Displays the IP address of the VPN Service Edge to which your traffic is being forwarded.
This field displays as Network Service Edge in previous versions of Zscaler Client Connector.
Client IP: Displays the IP address assigned to your device by the VPN Service Edge for the session.
Total Bytes Sent: Displays, in real time, bytes of traffic sent from your computer through the VPN Tunnel.
Total Bytes Received: Displays, in real time, bytes of traffic received from your computer through the VPN Tunnel.

evidence.after: This window includes the following features on macOS devices.
quotes: This section displays only if you are connected to the Zscaler cloud using a VPN connection.

zdx-window.statement: The Classic Digital Experience window on Windows shows Service Status, where Turn Off turns off the Z-Tunnel and disables the Digital Experience service while the user stays logged in, until Turn On; Authentication Status; Server; Time Connected; and ZDX Service Version. Its troubleshooting actions are Clear ZDX Data, to clear the ZDX data the app stored, and Restart ZDX Service, which on Android 3.8 and later and on Android on ChromeOS 3.8 and later can be tapped only once within a 30-second period. In the Modern UI, Clear removes historical data collected by Digital Experience and Restart restarts the core services for Digital Experience monitoring.

quotes: Service Status: Displays the app connection status. Tap Turn Off if you want to turn off the Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel) and disable the Digital Experience (i.e., ZDX) service while remaining logged in to the app.
The Digital Experience service is disabled until you tap Turn On.
Authentication Status: Displays the current authentication state, i.e., whether you are currently authenticated or not.
Server: Displays the IP Address of the server to which your traffic is being forwarded.
Time Connected: Displays your initial connection time for the present session.
ZDX Service Version: Displays the ZDX version your organization is using.
Clear ZDX Data: Tap to clear the ZDX data that Zscaler Client Connector stored.
Restart ZDX Service: Tap to restart the ZDX service.
You can tap Restart ZDX Service only once within a 30-second period. Applies to Zscaler Client Connector version 3.8 and later for Android.
You can tap Restart ZDX Service only once within a 30-second period. Applies to Zscaler Client Connector version 3.8 and later for Android on ChromeOS.
Clear ZDX Data: Click Clear to remove historical data collected by Digital Experience.
Restart ZDX Services: Click Restart to restart the core services for Digital Experience monitoring.

data-protection-window.statement: The Data Protection window, for Windows and macOS devices, shows connectivity information and troubleshooting steps for the Data Protection feature, including Product Version, the current version of the feature. The service can be disabled with the Password to Disable Endpoint DLP in App Profiles or with a one-time password, which is the password listed under Disable Endpoint DLP OTP in Compliance Status.

quotes: This window features connectivity information and troubleshooting steps for the Data Protection feature on Windows and macOS devices.
You can disable the service using the Password to Disable Endpoint DLP in App Profiles or by using a One-Time Password (OTP).
Product Version: Displays the current version of the Data Protection feature.

evidence.after: You can disable the service using the Password to Disable Endpoint DLP
quotes: Under Compliance Status, copy the password listed under Disable Endpoint DLP OTP.

dlp-integration-versions.statement: The Client Connector Endpoint DLP integration page says the feature is supported on devices running Client Connector 4.3 and later for Windows and 4.2 and later for macOS, and that it is only supported on macOS Monterey (12) and later.

quotes: This feature is supported on devices running Zscaler Client Connector version 4.3 and later for Windows and Zscaler Client Connector version 4.2 and later for macOS.
The Endpoint DLP feature is only supported on devices running macOS Monterey (12) and later versions.

dlp-data-protection-page.statement: An admin can enable Endpoint DLP using the Client Connector Portal; the page points to Configuring Client Connector Profiles for the steps to enable the Install Endpoint DLP feature. In the app, the Data Protection page refers to the Endpoint DLP feature, where end users can view the connection status of the service and perform troubleshooting.

quotes: Admin can enable Zscaler Endpoint DLP using the Zscaler Client Connector Portal.
For steps to enable the Install Endpoint DLP feature, see Configuring Zscaler Client Connector Profiles.
On Zscaler Client Connector, the Data Protection page refers to the Zscaler Endpoint DLP feature.
On the Data Protection page, the end-users can view the connection status of the service and perform troubleshooting.

dlp-notifications.statement: When a user violates an Endpoint DLP rule and user notifications are enabled, the user receives a message on the endpoint based on the triggered rule. For the Allow notification the user can click Learn more or Do Not Disturb, and it disappears automatically in 10 seconds; for the Block notification the user can click Learn more and then, under the More options drop-down menu, choose Do Not Disturb or Request Exemption; if the admin has set rules with a confirm action, end users receive a Confirm notification requesting action, and the user has 5 minutes to select an option, after which Zscaler blocks the activity.

quotes: When a user violates an Endpoint DLP rule, and the user notifications are enabled, they receive a message on the endpoint based on the triggered rule.

The user can click Learn more for more details about the notification or click Do Not Disturb to prevent the notification from reappearing. The allow notification automatically disappears in 10 seconds.
The user can click Learn more to understand why their activity was blocked, and then click the More options drop-down menu and choose Do Not Disturb or Request Exemption.
Confirm notification
If the admin has set rules with a confirm action, end users receive a notification requesting action.
The user has 5 minutes to select an option. If the user doesn’t provide input within the time period, Zscaler blocks the user activity.

dlp-mute.statement: Users can turn off Endpoint DLP user notifications under Zscaler Client Connector > More > Settings > Show all notifications; even then the Endpoint DLP notifications are still logged on the Notifications page.

quotes: Users can turn off Endpoint DLP user notifications on the Zscaler Client Connector > More > Settings >Show all notifications.
Even if this setting is turned off, the Endpoint DLP notifications are still logged on the Notifications page.

dlp-exemption.statement: A user blocked by Endpoint DLP for a rule violation can request an exemption from the block action and be monitored instead. In the Classic UI, Request exemption prompts for a password, the one-time password also works in offline mode, and the page says exemptions are granted for 12 hours. In the Modern UI the user enables the option, enters a Disable Reason on the Request exemption window and clicks Continue, might be prompted for a password, and a granted exemption shows a message that traffic is monitored but not blocked with an expiration time that the page gives as 12 hours after the exemption is granted.

quotes: Request exemption: Users that are blocked by the Endpoint DLP due to a rule violation can request to be exempted from the block action, and instead be monitored.
Clicking this option prompts you to enter a password.
The OTP also works if you are in offline mode. Exemptions are granted for 12 hours.
To request an exemption, enable this option, enter a Disable Reason on the Request exemption window, and click Continue. You might be prompted to enter a password.
If the exemption is granted, a message displays that indicates traffic is monitored but not blocked and provides the expiration time (12 hours after the exemption is granted).

dlp-policy-and-quarantine.statement: The Endpoint DLP policy refreshes every 15 minutes, and Update DLP Policy refreshes it immediately. Open Quarantine Folder contains files moved there as a result of a block action for the personal cloud storage rules (for example Dropbox) or by other channels where the file source information is missing (for example copying an extracted ZIP file to a removable storage device).

quotes: The DLP policy refreshes every 15 minutes. If you want to update immediately, click Update DLP Policy.

Open Quarantine Folder: Contains the files that moved to this folder as a result of a block action for the personal cloud storage rules (e.g., Dropbox) or by other channels where the file source information is missing (e.g., copying an extract ZIP file to a removable storage device).

endpoint-dlp-macos-floor.summary: The Client Connector Endpoint DLP integration page says Endpoint DLP is only supported on macOS Monterey (12) and later; the ZIA step-by-step Endpoint DLP page lists endpoints running macOS 14, 15 or 26.

quotes: The Endpoint DLP feature is only supported on devices running macOS Monterey (12) and later versions.

positions.says: Endpoint DLP is only supported on devices running macOS Monterey (12) and later versions.

quotes: Endpoints running macOS 14, 15, or 26 (Sonoma, Sequoia, or Tahoe)

positions.says: The prerequisites list endpoints running macOS 14, 15, or 26 (Sonoma, Sequoia, or Tahoe) (existing claim zia.dlp.endpoint-enforcement:prerequisites).

endpoint-dlp-macos-floor.impact: The oldest macOS release Endpoint DLP supports is Monterey (12) on one page and 14 on the other; the pages do not say whether the second is a list of tested releases or a floor.

dlp-block-trigger.summary: Inside the Endpoint DLP integration page, the Allow notification and the Block notification are each introduced with the same trigger, a rule configured for the Allow action.

quotes: When a user violates or triggers an Endpoint DLP rule that is configured for the Allow action and the End User Notification is selected as Show, the Allow notification is displayed.

positions.says: The Allow notification is displayed for a rule configured for the Allow action with the End User Notification set to Show.

quotes: When a user violates or triggers an Endpoint DLP rule that is configured for the Allow action and the End User Notification is selected as Show, the Block notification is displayed.

positions.says: The Block notification is displayed for a rule configured for the Allow action with the End User Notification set to Show, which repeats the Allow notification's trigger.

dlp-block-trigger.impact: The page does not state what rule configuration produces the Block notification, so it cannot be used to say when a user sees it.

exemption-duration.summary: The Classic and Modern end-user Endpoint DLP pages give the exemption as 12 hours, while the Endpoint Data Scan settings page makes the Exemption Duration selectable from 5 minutes to 12 hours.

quotes: The OTP also works if you are in offline mode. Exemptions are granted for 12 hours.

positions.says: Classic UI: exemptions are granted for 12 hours.

quotes: If the exemption is granted, a message displays that indicates traffic is monitored but not blocked and provides the expiration time (12 hours after the exemption is granted).

positions.says: Modern UI: the expiration time is 12 hours after the exemption is granted.

quotes: You can set the duration of 5 Minutes, 10 Minutes, 15 Minutes, 60 Minutes, 2 Hours, 6 Hours, or 12 Hours.

positions.says: The console's Exemption Duration can be set to 5 Minutes, 10 Minutes, 15 Minutes, 60 Minutes, 2 Hours, 6 Hours or 12 Hours (existing claim zia.dlp.endpoint-settings:exemption-duration).

exemption-duration.impact: An exemption length other than 12 hours is configurable on the console page but stated as a fixed 12 hours on both end-user pages; the pages do not say whether the end-user text assumes the maximum setting or ignores the setting.
